projects.title: Focus
projects.shortDescription: AI application that generates personalised short-form learning videos end to end.
projects.description: An educational application that turns a topic into a finished, narrated, captioned short-form video. A generation pipeline writes the script, synthesises the voice, times the captions, selects the visual format and renders the result — then serves it inside a mobile experience built around the pipeline rather than bolted onto it.
projects.contribution: Co-founder and developer. Designed and built the generation pipeline and the application around it.
verifiedFacts: Co-founded and built an AI application generating personalised short-form learning videos.
Pipeline runs prompt → script → voice → captions → visual composition → rendered video.
Supports multiple visual formats over a single content model.
Mobile experience sits on top of automated rendering pipelines.

presentation.concept: A phone plays a generated learning short. Scroll freezes it and explodes the frame into its ten production layers — script, model, content, voice, audio, characters, motion, captions, renderer, app — suspended in depth. The camera travels between layers while each one runs its real behaviour: the script types, the waveform speaks, the captions time themselves to it. Scrolling on recombines the stack into the finished video.
presentation.interaction: Scroll drives the explode/recombine. Hovering a layer isolates it and dims the rest. The phone is scrubbable.

projects.title: Gym App

Every exercise is a data record that drives the same model, rather than a separate asset — so the library scales without the download size scaling with it.

The 3D asset is loaded once and re-posed, never duplicated per exercise.

projects.title: Chess Assistant
projects.shortDescription: CNNs locate a chessboard on screen and classify every piece, then Stockfish suggests the move.
projects.description: A computer-vision pipeline that reads a chess position from pixels. One network regresses the board corners out of a full screenshot; a second classifies each of the 64 squares into thirteen classes. The reconstructed position is serialised to FEN and handed to Stockfish, which returns the best move. Training data is synthetic — boards composited onto generated desktops at random positions, sizes and themes, so the detector generalises past any one client.
projects.contribution: Full pipeline: dataset synthesis, both models, board reconstruction, engine integration and deployment.
verifiedFacts: Two trained models are committed to the repository: a per-square piece classifier and a board-corner regressor.
Piece classifier is a 3-block CNN (Conv2D 32/64/128 with max-pooling) → Flatten → Dense(128) → Dropout, on 64×64 crops.
Board localisation is solved as direct corner regression on a MobileNetV2 backbone at 384×384, refined by a local search.
Training data is synthetic: boards composited onto generated desktop wallpapers at random position, scale and theme.
Reconstructed positions are serialised to FEN and analysed by Stockfish via python-chess.
Thirteen piece classes (six white, six black, empty).

presentation.concept: The pipeline replays itself over a procedurally drawn desktop with a board composited onto it. A corner box snaps in and jitters through its refine search; a warped grid rectifies to a square; 64 crops fly out, get classified with confidence bars, and collapse into a FEN string; Stockfish thinks and draws the best move as an arc on a clean 3D board.
presentation.interaction: Scroll steps the pipeline. The board is playable at the end — an easter egg puzzle.

projects.title: Cinquillo 2.0
projects.shortDescription: A configurable card-game engine with MCTS and RL agents, used to design a measurably fairer game.
projects.description: A research project that treats game design as an optimisation problem. A fully parameterised Cinquillo engine exposes 33 named rule variants; Random, Heuristic, MCTS and reinforcement-learning agents play them at scale; and a 16-experiment pipeline measures how much of each outcome is skill and how much is seat order and deal luck. The output is not a bot — it is evidence for which rules make the game fair.
projects.contribution: Engine, agents, experiment harness and analysis.
verifiedFacts: Engine models the 40-card Spanish deck (Oros, Copas, Espadas, Bastos; ranks 1–7 and 10–12) with legality derived from board adjacency.
Moves are an abstract base class with PlayCard / RollDice / Pass subclasses — variants compose rather than fork.
33 named rule variants, including a fully parameterised dice mechanic with four beneficial and several adverse effects.
Agents span Random, Heuristic, Monte Carlo Tree Search and a reinforcement-learning agent.
RL agent uses a 209-feature state encoding, a 42-action Q-network and a 100,000-transition replay buffer.
16 simulation experiments, 5,000 games each by default.
README reports 260 passing tests.

presentation.concept: Four suit tracks run across the frame, each seeded by a glowing 5. A headless simulation deals outward from those seeds, cards snapping into slots with suit-coloured trails from the seat that played them, while seat rings shrink as hands empty. Below, a win-rate-by-seat bar chart converges live — visibly unfair under the base rules, visibly flattening when a variant is switched on.
presentation.interaction: Toggle rule variants and watch the fairness bars re-converge. Change the agent playing each seat.

projects.title: Stock Market Simulator
projects.shortDescription: Multithreaded Java limit-order-book simulator with a price-time matching engine.
projects.description: Trader threads place market and limit orders against independent per-symbol order books. A matching engine enforces price-time priority, executes crossing orders at the resting order’s limit price, re-rests unfilled remainder, and tracks position and PnL — all while a price engine walks each symbol under a Gaussian random walk and a JavaFX dashboard renders it live.
projects.contribution: Whole system: order books, matching engine, price engine, threading model and dashboard.
verifiedFacts: Order book implements price-time priority with two priority queues and explicit comparators.
Matching engine executes crossing limit orders at the resting order’s limit price and re-rests the remainder.
Price engine applies a geometric random walk per tick (≈0.1% standard deviation) at 5 ticks per second.
Concurrency via java.util.concurrent with a ScheduledExecutorService driving ticks.
Live JavaFX dashboard renders books, fills and PnL as the simulation runs.
Pluggable trader strategies, each running on its own thread.

metrics.label: Concurrent trades handled
metrics.note: Stated on CV; the repository configures 4 trader threads at 5 ticks/sec.

presentation.concept: A depth ladder with a drifting mid-price line. Order tiles slide in from both edges and stack into price levels; when a bid and an ask cross, they annihilate in a flash and the trade tape scrolls. The counter climbs 1 → 10 → 100 → 1K → 10K → 40K+ as scroll velocity increases, and the trader threads render as parallel lanes so concurrency is visible rather than described.
presentation.interaction: Scroll velocity drives order rate. Hover a price level to freeze and inspect it.

projects.title: Keyframes
projects.shortDescription: Editorial platform for motion-graphics work, with a moderated public submission pipeline.
projects.description: A full-stack catalogue of motion-graphics work: a filterable public grid with hover previews and detail pages, a public suggestion form, and a private back-office where an editor approves a suggestion into a live record. The interesting parts are defensive — an allow-listed embed builder, a four-gate upload validator, and accent-insensitive search that works identically on SQLite and Postgres.
projects.contribution: Sole author. Monorepo, API, database design, front-end and admin.
verifiedFacts: npm-workspaces monorepo: an Express + Prisma API and a React 19 + Vite front end sharing type, constant and embed modules.
Six Prisma models, with parallel SQLite and PostgreSQL schemas kept behaviourally identical (no native enums, JSON columns or scalar lists).
Accent- and case-insensitive search without Postgres-only features: rows store a pre-normalised search haystack and queries normalise the needle identically.
Video embeds never take an editor-supplied URL: the host is matched against an allow-list, the id validated per provider, and the embed URL rebuilt from a fixed template.
Uploads pass four independent gates — declared MIME, matching extension, byte size, and a real magic-byte signature check after write.
Helmet CSP configured with useDefaults: false and an explicit directive set; the uploads directory gets its own tighter policy.
Auth is a JWT in an httpOnly SameSite cookie with bcrypt hashes; the seed script creates no user and there are no default credentials in the repo.
Editorial pages are database rows rendered as React elements from Markdown, so page copy cannot inject markup.

presentation.concept: A contact sheet where every tile is a tiny motion graphic drawn procedurally rather than an image — kinetic type bars, spinning wireframe extrusions, cross-fading mixes — so the grid literally is the thing the platform catalogues. Beneath it runs a keyframe timeline with a draggable playhead; scrubbing drives every tile from the same clock.
presentation.interaction: Drag the timeline playhead. Toggle filter chips and watch the grid re-sort physically.

projects.title: TappedIn
projects.shortDescription: Django job board that parses CVs with spaCy and scores candidate–role fit.
projects.description: A job board where the matching is the product. Uploaded CVs are parsed with spaCy and PDF extraction into structured skills; a weighted matcher scores each candidate against each role out of 100, separating required from preferred skills and reporting exactly which required skills are missing. Built by a team of six, with a test suite to match.
projects.contribution: Team of six. Contributed across the matching engine, CV parsing and application.
verifiedFacts: Match score is 0–100 and returns both matched skills and the list of missing required skills.
Required and preferred skills are weighted 70/30, with a contract-type match bonus.
CV parsing uses pdfplumber for text, PyMuPDF for validation and spaCy en_core_web_sm for entity extraction.
The matcher carries a hand-built skill-synonym table (js/javascript, k8s/kubernetes, ml/ai, ux/ui …).
333 test methods across 30 test files.
Seeded with 100 users, 200 jobs and 500 applications.

presentation.concept: A bipartite matching graph. A stylised CV page scans top to bottom under a sweep line, each recognised skill popping out as a labelled pill; the pills fly into a lattice between candidate chips on the left and job cards on the right, and edges light up weighted by the 70/30 rule while a score dial counts to its value.
presentation.interaction: Click a job card to re-run the match against it. Hover an edge to see which skills carried it.

projects.description: A tutoring scheduling platform with three roles, recurring lesson generation, timetable clash detection and invoicing. presentation.interaction: Switch recurrence mode and watch the grid re-fill. Drag a block to force a clash.

projects.title: Three Body Problem
projects.shortDescription: Gravity simulator with a velocity-Verlet integrator, six orbital presets and live energy readout.
projects.description: A three-body gravity simulator built on a velocity-Verlet integrator with gravitational softening, six named orbital presets, and a live total-energy readout that shows the integrator conserving energy — or failing to, when you push it. Zero dependencies.
projects.contribution: Sole author.
verifiedFacts: Integrator is velocity-Verlet: accelerations computed, positions advanced by v·dt + ½a·dt², accelerations recomputed, velocities corrected.
Gravitational softening avoids singular forces at close approach.
Pairwise force accumulation is O(n²) exploiting Newton’s third law reciprocity.
Six orbital presets, including the figure-eight solution.
Trails capped at 2,000 points; no runtime dependencies.

presentation.concept: The same velocity-Verlet integrator runs twice on identical figure-eight initial conditions, except one copy has a single body nudged by 1e-6. Both draw on the same axes as fading trails. For hundreds of steps they are pixel-identical; then they separate, and a log-scale divergence readout climbs beside them. Chaos, demonstrated rather than asserted.
presentation.interaction: Drag any body to perturb the system live. Reset to a preset.

projects.title: Labyrinth
projects.shortDescription: Maze generator and solver that animates eight classic search algorithms step by step.
projects.description: Three maze generators and eight search algorithms, all animated on the same grid so you can watch how differently they think. Recursive backtracker, Prim and Kruskal build; BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, A*, greedy best-first and others solve — and the difference between a breadth-first wavefront and an A* teardrop is immediately legible.
projects.contribution: Sole author.
verifiedFacts: Eight search algorithms and three maze generators.
Generators: iterative-DFS recursive backtracker, Prim, and Kruskal.
Kruskal is backed by a union-find structure with path compression and union by rank.
Grids up to 120×120. No JavaScript libraries.

presentation.concept: Three beats on one grid. The maze carves itself live under a recursive-backtracker cursor, its stack trailing as a ribbon that visibly pops back at dead ends. Then the finished maze floods twice at once from the same cell — BFS as a cool concentric wavefront, A* as a warm directed teardrop. Finally both paths draw, and the node counts settle side by side.
presentation.interaction: Pick an algorithm and re-run. Drag the start or goal cell.

projects.title: Encrypted Proxy VPN
projects.shortDescription: Fernet-encrypted TCP relay and local HTTP proxy routing a remote device through a home machine.
projects.description: A working, minimal VPN: a threaded TCP relay on a home machine, a local HTTP proxy on the remote device, and Fernet symmetric encryption on the wire between them. Plus a browser-side detector page that measures whether traffic is actually going through the tunnel.
projects.contribution: Sole author. Server, client proxy, crypto layer and detector page.
verifiedFacts: Server binds a TCP socket with SO_REUSEADDR and spawns a daemon thread per connection.
Payloads are encrypted with Fernet (symmetric authenticated encryption) from the cryptography library.
Client runs a local HTTP proxy that forwards requests over the encrypted relay.
Includes a browser detector page that measures latency and connection routing.
No third-party dependency manifest — dependencies are declared in module docstrings.

presentation.concept: Three nodes — remote device, home server, open web — joined by two links. Packets stream from the device and visibly collapse from readable text into scrambled ciphertext with a padlock as they enter the tunnel, decrypt at the server, and continue in the clear. Toggling the tunnel off makes the packets stay readable the whole way.
presentation.interaction: Toggle the tunnel. Click a packet to inspect its plaintext and ciphertext.

projects.title: Minecraft Seed Finder
projects.shortDescription: Brute-force search for Minecraft seeds whose strongholds are ringed by specific structures.
projects.description: A brute-force seed search over Minecraft’s world generation. Python drives four generated C programs built against the Cubiomes library, scanning ten thousand regions per seed to find worlds where a stronghold sits within 500 blocks of a required set of structures.
projects.contribution: Sole author.
verifiedFacts: Python writes four complete C programs into a Cubiomes checkout, compiles them, and drives them as subprocesses.
All four C programs target Minecraft 1.21 world generation.
Scans 10,201 overworld regions per query and 90,601 nether regions for fortress queries.
Structure distance limit of 500 blocks around each of three checked strongholds.

presentation.concept: A top-down region grid with a stronghold spiral fixed at centre and dashed radius rings at 100 and 500 blocks. A scan cursor sweeps outward exactly as the C loops do, cells flashing as they are visited; viable regions pop a structure glyph. When a seed satisfies every constraint the whole grid flashes and the seed number locks in.
presentation.interaction: Change the required structures and re-run the scan.
